s.t: A duck built a nest by the water.
s.fr: Un canard construisit un nid près de l’eau.

s.t: She laid many eggs in the nest.
s.fr: Elle pondit beaucoup d’œufs dans le nid.

s.t: Every day, she sat on her eggs.
s.fr: Chaque jour, elle s’assit sur ses œufs.

s.t: One egg was bigger than the other eggs.
s.fr: Un œuf était plus grand que les autres œufs.

s.t: "Whose big egg is this?" an old duck asked.
s.fr: « À qui est ce gros œuf ? » demanda une vieille cane.

s.t: The mother duck did not know whose egg it was.
s.fr: La mère cane ne savait pas à qui appartenait cet œuf.

paras.summary: A duck builds a nest by the water and lays many eggs, sitting on them every day; one egg is bigger than the other eggs, and an old duck asks whose big egg it is.

s.t: She said nothing more.
s.fr: Elle ne dit rien de plus.

s.t: Soon the smaller eggs began to crack open.
s.fr: Bientôt les petits œufs commencèrent à se fissurer.

s.t: Small yellow ducklings came out.
s.fr: De petits canetons jaunes sortirent.

s.t: The small ducklings sat by the nest.
s.fr: Les petits canetons s’assirent près du nid.

paras.summary: The mother duck says nothing more, and soon the smaller eggs crack open into small yellow ducklings, who sit by the nest.

s.t: The mother duck came to the nest every day.
s.fr: La mère cane vint au nid chaque jour.

s.t: But the big egg did not crack yet.
s.fr: Mais le gros œuf ne se fissura pas encore.

s.t: The mother duck sat on the big egg again.
s.fr: La mère cane s’assit de nouveau sur le grand œuf.

s.t: She waited for the big one to open.
s.fr: Elle attendit que le grand s’ouvre.

paras.summary: The mother duck comes to the nest every day, but the big egg does not crack yet, so she sits on it again and waits for it to open.

s.t: At last, the big egg began to crack.
s.fr: Enfin, le grand œuf commença à se fissurer.

s.t: A gray duckling came out of the egg.
s.fr: Un caneton gris sortit de l’œuf.

s.t: The other ducklings were small and yellow.
s.fr: Les autres canetons étaient petits et jaunes.

s.t: This duckling was big and gray.
s.fr: Ce caneton était grand et gris.

s.t: "This duckling is not pretty," an old duck said.
s.fr: « Ce caneton n’est pas joli, » dit une vieille cane.

s.t: "But he is still my child," the mother duck said.
s.fr: « Mais il est quand-même mon enfant, » dit la mère cane.

paras.summary: At last the big egg cracks open, and a gray duckling comes out, big and gray next to the other small, yellow ducklings; an old duck says he is not pretty, but the mother duck says he is still her child.

s.t: The next day, the mother duck took her ducklings to the water.
s.fr: Le lendemain, la mère cane emmena ses canetons à l’eau.

s.t: One by one, the ducklings went into the water.
s.fr: Un par un, les canetons entrèrent dans l’eau.

s.t: The gray duckling went into the water too.
s.fr: Le caneton gris entra dans l’eau lui aussi.

s.t: He swam better than the other ducklings.
s.fr: Il nageait mieux que les autres canetons.

paras.summary: The next day the mother duck takes her ducklings to the water; one by one they go in, and the gray duckling goes in too, swimming better than the other ducklings.

s.t: Even the old duck watched him swim.
s.fr: Même le vieux canard le regarda nager.

s.t: "This duckling swims very well," the mother duck said.
s.fr: « Ce caneton nage très bien, » dit la mère canard.

s.t: She was proud of the gray duckling.
s.fr: Elle était fière du caneton gris.

s.t: Soon she would take her ducklings to the farmyard.
s.fr: Bientôt elle emmènerait ses canetons à la basse-cour.

paras.summary: Even the old duck watches him swim, and the mother duck says he swims very well; proud of him, she plans to take her ducklings to the farmyard soon.

s.t: The mother duck took her ducklings to the farmyard.
s.fr: La mère canard emmena ses canetons à la basse-cour.

s.t: Many other ducks lived in the farmyard.
s.fr: Beaucoup d’autres canards vivaient dans la basse-cour.

s.t: The other ducks saw the gray duckling.
s.fr: Les autres canards virent le caneton gris.

s.t: "Look at that ugly duckling!" one duck said.
s.fr: « Regardez ce vilain caneton ! » dit un canard.

s.t: "He is too big for a duckling," said another duck.
s.fr: « Il est trop grand pour un caneton, » dit un autre canard.

s.t: The ducks did not want him near them.
s.fr: Les canards ne voulaient pas qu’il s’approche d’eux.

paras.summary: The mother duck takes her ducklings to the farmyard, where many other ducks live and see the gray duckling; one duck calls him ugly, and another says he is too big, so the ducks do not want him near them.

s.t: One duck bit his neck.
s.fr: Un canard lui mordit le cou.

s.t: "Go away, ugly duckling!" the duck said.
s.fr: « Va-t-en, vilain caneton ! » dit le canard.

s.t: The other ducklings went to play in the farmyard.
s.fr: Les autres canetons allèrent jouer dans la basse-cour.

s.t: But no duck would play with the gray duckling.
s.fr: Mais aucun canard ne voulut jouer avec le caneton gris.

s.t: He walked alone.
s.fr: Il marcha seul.

s.t: He put his head down and said nothing.
s.fr: Il baissa la tête et ne dit rien.

paras.summary: One duck bites his neck and tells him to go away, and while the other ducklings go to play in the farmyard, no duck will play with the gray duckling, so he walks alone with his head down, saying nothing.

s.t: Hens lived in the farmyard too.
s.fr: Des poules vivaient dans la basse-cour aussi.

s.t: The hens looked at the gray duckling.
s.fr: Les poules regardèrent le caneton gris.

s.t: "That duckling is strange," one hen said.
s.fr: « Ce caneton est étrange, » dit une poule.

s.t: "He is too big and too gray," said another hen.
s.fr: « Il est trop grand et trop gris, » dit une autre poule.

s.t: The hens went away from him.
s.fr: Les poules s’éloignèrent de lui.

s.t: A girl fed the ducks and hens every day.
s.fr: Une fille nourrissait les canards et les poules chaque jour.

paras.summary: Hens live in the farmyard too, and they look at the gray duckling and call him strange, too big, and too gray, so the hens go away from him.

s.t: The girl saw the gray duckling.
s.fr: La fille vit le caneton gris.

s.t: She kicked him away from the food.
s.fr: Elle le chassa loin de la nourriture.

s.t: "Go away, you ugly duckling," she said.
s.fr: « Va-t’en, vilain caneton, » dit-elle.

s.t: The gray duckling went hungry that day.
s.fr: Le caneton gris souffrit de la faim ce jour-là.

paras.summary: A girl who feeds the ducks and hens every day sees the gray duckling and kicks him away from the food, calling him an ugly duckling, so he goes hungry.

s.t: His mother grew tired of him too.
s.fr: Sa mère se lassa de lui aussi.

s.t: "I wish you were far from here," she said.
s.fr: « Je voudrais que tu sois loin d’ici, » dit-elle.

s.t: The duckling heard what she said.
s.fr: Le caneton entendit ce qu’elle dit.

s.t: He walked away with his head down.
s.fr: Il s’en alla la tête baissée.

paras.summary: Even his mother grows tired of him and says she wishes he were far from here, and the duckling, hearing her words, walks away with his head down.

s.t: The duckling left the farmyard.
s.fr: Le caneton quitta la basse-cour.

s.t: No duck or hen wanted him near them.
s.fr: Aucun canard ni poule ne voulait l’avoir près d’eux.

s.t: He walked far from the farmyard.
s.fr: Il marcha loin de la basse-cour.

s.t: He walked all night long.
s.fr: Il marcha toute la nuit.

paras.summary: The duckling leaves the farmyard, since no duck or hen wants him near them, and he walks far from the farmyard, all night long.

s.t: In the morning, he came to a big marsh.
s.fr: Le matin, il arriva à un grand marais.

s.t: Wild birds lived in the marsh.
s.fr: Des oiseaux sauvages vivaient dans le marais.

s.t: Tall reeds grew by the marsh.
s.fr: De grands roseaux poussaient près du marais.

s.t: The marsh was new to him.
s.fr: Le marais lui était inconnu.

s.t: He looked at the wide water.
s.fr: Il regarda l’eau large.

s.t: He was tired from his long walk.
s.fr: Il était fatigué de sa longue marche.

s.t: He sat down near the water to rest.
s.fr: Il s’assit près de l’eau pour se reposer.

paras.summary: In the morning he comes to a big marsh, where wild birds live and tall reeds grow by the marsh, all new to him; after he looks at the wide water, tired from his long walk, he sits down near the water to rest.

s.t: Wild geese lived in the marsh too.
s.fr: Des oies sauvages vivaient aussi dans le marais.

s.t: The duckling stayed near the reeds.
s.fr: Le caneton resta près des roseaux.

s.t: He said nothing to the wild geese.
s.fr: Il ne dit rien aux oies sauvages.

s.t: The wild geese said nothing to him either.
s.fr: Les oies sauvages ne lui dirent rien non plus.

paras.summary: Wild geese live in the marsh too, but the duckling stays near the reeds and says nothing to them, and the wild geese say nothing to him either.

s.t: One night, loud sounds came from the marsh.
s.fr: Une nuit, de forts bruits vinrent du marais.

s.t: Hunters came to the marsh with guns.
s.fr: Des chasseurs vinrent au marais avec des fusils.

s.t: The hunters shot at the wild birds.
s.fr: Les chasseurs tirèrent sur les oiseaux sauvages.

s.t: Big dogs ran through the reeds and water.
s.fr: De grands chiens couraient à travers les roseaux et l’eau.

s.t: The duckling sat in the tall reeds.
s.fr: Le caneton était assis dans les grands roseaux.

paras.summary: One night, loud sounds come from the marsh: hunters come with guns and shoot at the wild birds, and big dogs run through the reeds and water, so the duckling sits still in the tall reeds.

s.t: A big dog came close to him.
s.fr: Un grand chien s’approcha de lui.

s.t: The dog looked at him but did not bite him.
s.fr: Le chien le regarda mais ne le mordit pas.

s.t: The duckling was so ugly that no dog would bite him.
s.fr: Le caneton était si laid qu’aucun chien ne voulait le mordre.

s.t: At last, the hunters and dogs went away.
s.fr: Enfin, les chasseurs et les chiens partirent.

s.t: The duckling was alone in the marsh again.
s.fr: Le caneton était de nouveau seul dans le marais.

paras.summary: A big dog comes close and looks at him but does not bite him, for the duckling is so ugly that no dog would bite him; at last the hunters and dogs go away, and the duckling is alone in the marsh again.

s.t: The days grew cold.
s.fr: Les jours devinrent froids.

s.t: The duckling was cold and alone.
s.fr: Le caneton avait froid et était seul.

s.t: One day, he left the marsh.
s.fr: Un jour, il quitta le marais.

s.t: He walked all day.
s.fr: Il marcha toute la journée.

s.t: At night, he came to a small hut.
s.fr: La nuit, il arriva à une petite cabane.

paras.summary: The days grow cold, and the duckling, cold and alone, leaves the marsh and walks all day, coming to a small hut at night.

s.t: An old woman lived in the hut.
s.fr: Une vieille femme vivait dans la hutte.

s.t: The old woman found the duckling, tired and cold.
s.fr: La vieille femme trouva le caneton, fatigué et froid.

s.t: The old woman could not see well.
s.fr: La vieille femme ne voyait pas bien.

s.t: "You may stay here," the old woman said.
s.fr: « Vous pouvez rester ici, » dit la vieille femme.

s.t: She thought the duckling could lay eggs.
s.fr: Elle pensait que le caneton pouvait pondre des œufs.

s.t: A hen and a cat lived in the hut.
s.fr: Une poule et un chat vivaient dans la hutte.

s.t: The duckling would stay with them.
s.fr: Le caneton resterait avec eux.

paras.summary: An old woman lives in the hut and finds the duckling, tired and cold; she cannot see well, so she tells him he may stay, thinking he could lay eggs, and the duckling would stay with her hen and cat.

s.t: The hen and the cat lived well in the hut.
s.fr: La poule et le chat vivaient bien dans la hutte.

s.t: The cat could arch his back and purr.
s.fr: Le chat pouvait arquer le dos et ronronner.

s.t: The hen could lay eggs every day.
s.fr: La poule pouvait pondre des œufs chaque jour.

s.t: "Can you lay eggs?" the hen asked the duckling.
s.fr: « Pouvez-vous pondre des œufs ? » demanda la poule au caneton.

s.t: "No, I cannot," said the duckling.
s.fr: « Non, je ne peux pas, » dit le caneton.

paras.summary: The hen and the cat live well in the hut, for the cat can arch his back and purr, and the hen can lay eggs every day; but when the hen asks if the duckling can lay eggs, he says no.

s.t: "Can you purr like the cat?" the hen asked.
s.fr: « Peux-tu ronronner comme le chat ? » demanda la poule.

s.t: "No, I cannot do that either," said the duckling.
s.fr: « Non, je ne peux pas faire cela non plus, » dit le caneton.

s.t: "You have no right to talk," said the cat.
s.fr: « Tu n’as pas le droit de parler, » dit le chat.

s.t: The duckling said nothing more.
s.fr: Le caneton ne dit plus rien.

paras.summary: The hen asks if he can purr like the cat, and he says he cannot do that either, so the cat says he has no right to talk, and the duckling says nothing.

s.t: He thought of the wild marsh again.
s.fr: Il pensa de nouveau au marais sauvage.

s.t: He wanted to swim in the water.
s.fr: Il voulait nager dans l’eau.

s.t: "Swimming is a foolish wish," the hen said.
s.fr: « Nager est un désir stupide, » dit la poule.

s.t: The cat did not want him to swim either.
s.fr: Le chat ne voulait pas non plus qu’il nage.

s.t: But the duckling still wanted to swim.
s.fr: Mais le caneton voulait encore nager.

s.t: He knew he would leave the hut.
s.fr: Il savait qu’il quitterait la cabane.

paras.summary: He thinks of the wild marsh again and wants to swim in the water, but the hen calls swimming a foolish wish, and the cat does not want him to swim either; still, the duckling wants to swim, and he knows he would leave the hut.

s.t: The duckling left the hut.
s.fr: Le caneton quitta la cabane.

s.t: He did not go back to the marsh.
s.fr: Il ne retourna pas au marais.

s.t: He found a big lake.
s.fr: Il trouva un grand lac.

s.t: The lake had wide water.
s.fr: Le lac avait une eau large.

s.t: The duckling swam into the water.
s.fr: Le caneton nagea dans l’eau.

s.t: He dove under the water too.
s.fr: Il plongea aussi sous l’eau.

s.t: No one there called him ugly.
s.fr: Personne là-bas ne l’appela laid.

paras.summary: The duckling leaves the hut, not going back to the marsh, and finds a big lake with wide water; he swims into the water and dives under it too, and no one there calls him ugly.

s.t: The duckling swam every day.
s.fr: Le caneton nageait chaque jour.

s.t: He dove and swam alone.
s.fr: Il plongea et nagea seul.

s.t: Other birds saw him but did not come near.
s.fr: D’autres oiseaux le virent mais ne s’approchèrent pas.

s.t: The duckling stayed on the lake all day.
s.fr: Le caneton resta sur le lac toute la journée.

s.t: He loved the open water.
s.fr: Il aimait l’eau ouverte.

s.t: The leaves began to fall.
s.fr: Les feuilles commencèrent à tomber.

s.t: The autumn days grew colder.
s.fr: Les jours d’automne devinrent plus froids.

paras.summary: The duckling swims every day, diving and swimming alone, and though other birds see him, they do not come near; still, he stays on the lake all day and loves the open water, even as the leaves begin to fall and the autumn days grow colder.

s.t: One autumn day, the duckling swam on the lake.
s.fr: Un jour d’automne, le caneton nagea sur le lac.

s.t: He saw big white birds in the sky.
s.fr: Il vit de grands oiseaux blancs dans le ciel.

s.t: The birds had long necks and white feathers.
s.fr: Les oiseaux avaient de longs cous et des plumes blanches.

s.t: They were swans, and they flew south.
s.fr: C’étaient des cygnes, et ils volèrent vers le sud.

s.t: The swans called to one another as they flew.
s.fr: Les cygnes s’appelaient l’un l’autre pendant qu’ils volaient.

s.t: The swans flew near the lake.
s.fr: Les cygnes volèrent près du lac.

paras.summary: One autumn day, the duckling swims on the lake when he sees big white birds in the sky, birds with long necks and white feathers; they are swans, flying south and calling to one another near the lake.

s.t: The duckling had not seen birds so beautiful.
s.fr: Le caneton n’avait pas vu d’oiseaux si beaux.

s.t: He watched the swans fly away.
s.fr: Il regarda les cygnes s’éloigner.

s.t: The duckling wanted to follow the swans.
s.fr: Le caneton voulait suivre les cygnes.

s.t: He did not know why.
s.fr: Il ne savait pas pourquoi.

paras.summary: The duckling has not seen birds so beautiful, and he watches them fly away, wanting to follow them though he does not know why.

s.t: The duckling swam alone again.
s.fr: Le caneton nagea de nouveau seul.

s.t: He thought of the beautiful white swans.
s.fr: Il pensa aux beaux cygnes blancs.

s.t: Soon the days grew even colder.
s.fr: Les jours devinrent bientôt encore plus froids.

s.t: The water was cold and gray.
s.fr: L’eau était froide et grise.

paras.summary: He swims alone again, thinking of the beautiful white swans, as the days grow even colder and the water turns cold and gray.

s.t: Winter came.
s.fr: L’hiver arriva.

s.t: Ice grew on the lake.
s.fr: De la glace se forma sur le lac.

s.t: Every day, the ice grew thick.
s.fr: Chaque jour, la glace devenait épaisse.

s.t: Other birds flew away for the winter.
s.fr: D’autres oiseaux s’envolèrent pour l’hiver.

s.t: The duckling was alone on the lake.
s.fr: Le caneton était seul sur le lac.

s.t: He thought of the beautiful swans again.
s.fr: Il pensa de nouveau aux beaux cygnes.

paras.summary: Winter comes, and ice grows on the lake, thick every day, so that other birds fly away for the winter; the duckling is alone on the lake, and he thinks of the beautiful swans again.

s.t: Still, he swam to keep the water open.
s.fr: Pourtant, il nagea pour garder l’eau ouverte.

s.t: But the water grew smaller every day.
s.fr: Mais l’eau devenait plus petite chaque jour.

s.t: The duckling grew tired.
s.fr: Le caneton devint fatigué.

s.t: One cold night, he grew too tired to swim.
s.fr: Une nuit froide, il devint trop fatigué pour nager.

s.t: Soon he was frozen fast in the ice.
s.fr: Bientôt il fut gelé et figé dans la glace.

s.t: He could not move.
s.fr: Il ne pouvait pas bouger.

paras.summary: Still, he swims to keep the water open, but the water grows smaller every day, and the duckling grows tired, until one cold night he grows too tired to swim; soon he is frozen fast in the ice, unable to move.

s.t: A farmer walked by the frozen lake.
s.fr: Un fermier passa près du lac gelé.

s.t: He saw the duckling frozen in the ice.
s.fr: Il vit le caneton gelé dans la glace.

s.t: The farmer walked out on the ice.
s.fr: Le fermier marcha sur la glace.

s.t: He broke the ice with his shoe.
s.fr: Il brisa la glace avec son soulier.

s.t: The farmer took the duckling.
s.fr: Le fermier prit le caneton.

s.t: The duckling could not move.
s.fr: Le caneton ne pouvait pas bouger.

s.t: His feathers were wet and cold.
s.fr: Ses plumes étaient mouillées et froides.

paras.summary: A farmer walks by the frozen lake and sees the duckling frozen in the ice; he walks out on the ice and breaks it with his shoe, then takes the duckling, whose feathers are wet and cold and who cannot move.

s.t: The farmer was kind to birds.
s.fr: Le fermier était bon envers les oiseaux.

s.t: He carried the duckling to his wife.
s.fr: Il porta le caneton à sa femme.

s.t: "This bird is frozen," said the farmer.
s.fr: « Cet oiseau est gelé, » dit-il le fermier.

s.t: His wife took the duckling.
s.fr: Sa femme prit le caneton.

paras.summary: The farmer, who is kind to birds, carries the duckling to his wife, saying this bird is frozen, and his wife takes the duckling.

s.t: She put the duckling near the fire.
s.fr: Elle mit le caneton près du feu.

s.t: The duckling did not want to be there.
s.fr: Le caneton ne voulait pas être là.

s.t: He thought of the wild marsh.
s.fr: Il pensa au marais sauvage.

s.t: Soon the duckling began to move again.
s.fr: Bientôt le caneton recommença à bouger.

paras.summary: She puts the duckling near the fire, but the duckling does not want to be there and thinks of the wild marsh, until soon he begins to move again.

s.t: The farmer had children.
s.fr: Le fermier avait des enfants.

s.t: The children ran to see the duckling.
s.fr: Les enfants coururent voir le caneton.

s.t: "Look at that bird!" one child said.
s.fr: « Regardez cet oiseau ! » dit un enfant.

s.t: The children wanted to play with him.
s.fr: Les enfants voulaient jouer avec lui.

s.t: The duckling did not know the children.
s.fr: Le caneton ne connaissait pas les enfants.

s.t: He flew up on the table.
s.fr: Il vola sur la table.

s.t: The milk fell to the floor.
s.fr: Le lait tomba sur le sol.

paras.summary: The farmer has children, and they run to see the duckling, wanting to play with him, but the duckling does not know them, so he flies up on the table and knocks the milk to the floor.

s.t: The children called out.
s.fr: Les enfants appelèrent.

s.t: The farmer's wife ran in.
s.fr: La femme du fermier entra en courant.

s.t: The duckling flew into the flour.
s.fr: Le caneton vola dans la farine.

s.t: White flour was on his gray feathers.
s.fr: De la farine blanche était sur ses plumes grises.

s.t: But the duckling ran from her.
s.fr: Mais le caneton s’enfuit loin d’elle.

s.t: He ran through the door.
s.fr: Il courut par la porte.

s.t: He ran out into the cold.
s.fr: Il courut dehors dans le froid.

paras.summary: The children call out, and the farmer's wife runs in, but the duckling flies into the flour, and white flour lands on his gray feathers; still, he runs from her, through the door, and out into the cold.

s.t: The duckling ran far away.
s.fr: Le caneton courut très loin.

s.t: He found the reeds by the frozen lake.
s.fr: Il trouva les roseaux près du lac gelé.

s.t: He hid among the tall reeds.
s.fr: Il se cacha parmi les grands roseaux.

s.t: The winter was long.
s.fr: L’hiver fut long.

s.t: The duckling was cold every day.
s.fr: Le caneton avait froid chaque jour.

paras.summary: The duckling runs far away and finds the reeds by the frozen lake, hiding among the tall reeds through a long winter, cold for him every day.

s.t: He did not find much food.
s.fr: Il ne trouva pas grand-chose à manger.

s.t: No one came to see him.
s.fr: Personne ne vint le voir.

s.t: He stayed alone among the reeds.
s.fr: Il resta seul parmi les roseaux.

s.t: At last, the ice began to melt.
s.fr: Enfin, la glace commença à fondre.

s.t: The sun grew warm again.
s.fr: Le soleil redevint chaud.

s.t: The warm sun was on his feathers.
s.fr: Le soleil chaud était sur ses plumes.

paras.summary: He does not find much food, and no one comes to see him, so he stays alone among the reeds; at last the ice begins to melt, the sun grows warm again, and the warm sun is on his feathers.

s.t: The days grew warm again.
s.fr: Les jours redevinrent chauds.

s.t: The duckling had grown much bigger.
s.fr: Le caneton avait beaucoup grandi.

s.t: He could fly well.
s.fr: Il pouvait bien voler.

s.t: One day, he flew to the lake.
s.fr: Un jour, il vola jusqu’au lac.

s.t: He saw swans on the water.
s.fr: Il vit des cygnes sur l’eau.

s.t: The swans were big and white.
s.fr: Les cygnes étaient grands et blancs.

paras.summary: The days grow warm again; the duckling has grown much bigger and can fly well, and one day he flies to the lake and sees swans on the water.

s.t: The duckling wanted to swim with them.
s.fr: Le caneton voulait nager avec eux.

s.t: But he thought he was still gray and big.
s.fr: Mais il pensait qu’il était encore gris et grand.

s.t: He thought of the farmyard and the marsh.
s.fr: Il pensa à la basse-cour et au marais.

s.t: He thought of the hen and the cat too.
s.fr: Il pensa aussi à la poule et au chat.

s.t: "The swans may kill an ugly bird like me," he thought.
s.fr: « Les cygnes vont peut-être tuer un oiseau laid comme moi, » pensa-t-il.

s.t: "But I would rather die than be alone again," he thought.
s.fr: « Mais je préférerais mourir plutôt que d’être seul encore, » pensa-t-il.

s.t: He swam to the swans.
s.fr: Il nagea vers les cygnes.

paras.summary: The swans are big and white, and the duckling wants to swim with them, though he thinks he is still gray and big; he thinks of the farmyard, the marsh, the hen, and the cat, and thinks the swans may kill an ugly bird like him, but he would rather die than be alone again, so he swims to the swans.

s.t: The duckling swam close to the swans.
s.fr: Le caneton nagea près des cygnes.

s.t: He bowed his head and waited for them to attack.
s.fr: Il baissa la tête et attendit qu’ils l’attaquent.

s.t: But the swans did not attack him.
s.fr: Mais les cygnes ne l’attaquèrent pas.

s.t: The swans swam near him.
s.fr: Les cygnes nagèrent près de lui.

s.t: He looked down into the water.
s.fr: Il regarda en bas dans l’eau.

s.t: He saw his reflection in the water.
s.fr: Il vit son reflet dans l’eau.

paras.summary: The duckling swims close to the swans and bows his head, waiting for them to attack, but the swans do not attack him and swim near him instead, so he looks down into the water and sees his reflection there.

s.t: The reflection was not a gray duckling.
s.fr: Le reflet n’était pas un caneton gris.

s.t: It was a big, white swan.
s.fr: C’était un grand cygne blanc.

s.t: The duckling had become a swan too.
s.fr: Le caneton était devenu un cygne aussi.

s.t: Children played by the water.
s.fr: Des enfants jouaient près de l’eau.

paras.summary: The reflection is not a gray duckling but a big, white swan, for the duckling has become a swan too, and children playing by the water see him.

s.t: "Look at that new swan!" said one child.
s.fr: « Regardez ce nouveau cygne ! » dit-il un enfant.

s.t: "He is the most beautiful of all!" said another child.
s.fr: « Il est le plus beau de tous ! » dit un autre enfant.

s.t: The swan spread his wings.
s.fr: Le cygne déploya ses ailes.

s.t: He swam among the swans, one of them at last.
s.fr: Il nagea parmi les cygnes, l’un d’eux enfin.

paras.summary: One child calls him a new swan, and another calls him the most beautiful of all; the swan spreads his wings and swims among the swans, one of them at last.
